problem_statement: J0SUKE/vortex-gallery is a three.js/WebGL gallery built with Vite + TypeScript: a full-viewport fixed <canvas id="webgl"> renders a vortex ring built from a 20-image texture atlas (/frames/512/p1.jpg .. 20.jpg), advanced by a normalize-wheel scroll handler in canvas.ts/gallery.ts. Over the fixed scene floats the gallery's own foreground instrument, the 'Frame navigator' HUD (a .fnav panel mounted inside #app): an eyebrow wordmark, a 'Frame navigator' title, a four-tile status strip (Center frame / Direction / Atlas range / Source path), a row of frame-group buttons (All frames, Openers, Sequence, Finale) that jump the navigator between slices of the 20-frame atlas, and a readout beneath them that reads 'Now holding: All frames · 20 of 20 frames'. Because the WebGL surface is a fixed inset:0 layer that never scrolls, the Frame navigator panel is the only normal-flow foreground chrome and carries all responsive, visual, cross-context and interaction behaviour. The task is to finish the Frame navigator so it is a single coherent, legible, responsive instrument: (1) the four-tile status strip must wrap cleanly and never force horizontal overflow on a 390px phone; (2) the panel must stay legible and well-proportioned over the scene rather than overgrowing into oversized dark slabs that cascade, overlap and bury the vortex with dark-on-dark text; (3) the navigator must persist as the same instrument across every scroll context the visitor moves through (the initial view and the forward and reverse scroll contexts), not vanish after the initial view; and (4) picking a frame group in the selector must update the readout live (for example picking Finale must change the readout to 'Now holding: Finale · 7 of 20 frames'), not leave a frozen 'All frames' line while the button merely highlights. The WebGL canvas, the 20-image atlas, the wheel-driven vortex motion and the panel's copy and structure must remain fully intact.
required_content: The Frame navigator HUD (the .fnav panel) renders over the WebGL scene with its eyebrow wordmark, 'Frame navigator' title, four-tile status strip (Center frame / Direction / Atlas range / Source path), frame-group button row and readout, and stays legible and well-proportioned rather than overgrowing into oversized slabs that cascade, overlap and bury the vortex with illegible dark-on-dark text.
The four-tile status strip wraps cleanly and introduces no horizontal overflow of the foreground chrome on a 390px mobile viewport.

The Frame navigator persists as one consistent instrument across every scroll context the visitor moves through — the initial view and the forward and reverse scroll contexts — carrying its fnav--<context> tag on each, not appearing only on the initial view.

Selecting a frame group in the navigator updates the readout live to name the chosen group (for example 'Now holding: Finale · 7 of 20 frames'); the highlight and the readout stay in sync rather than the readout freezing on the initial 'All frames' line.
The WebGL canvas (#webgl), the 20-image texture atlas under /frames/512, and the wheel-driven vortex motion in canvas.ts/gallery.ts remain intact and error-free.
No console errors are introduced on any state; the swiftshader GL driver's intermittent shader-program parse messages under headless rendering are driver artifacts, not app errors.
design_constraints: Preserve the gallery's immersive full-viewport WebGL identity: the vortex fills the screen and the Frame navigator HUD remains the only foreground chrome, keeping the dark glass panel and the monospace type.

Do not convert the experience into a marketing landing page, dashboard, blog, or multi-section scrolling site; it must remain a single-route immersive WebGL gallery with a floating Frame navigator HUD.
The Frame navigator status strip must be a wrapping, self-clamping flex row (tiles flex 1 1 150px, min-width 0) so it never exceeds the mobile viewport width; do not use a fixed wide no-wrap row.
The navigator tiles, labels and values must keep sufficient contrast to stay legible over the scene; do not set near-black text on near-black tile fills or let tiles overlap one another.
The Frame navigator must be mounted in every scroll context (initial / forward / reverse), tagged with the matching fnav--<context> class, so it reads as one persistent instrument.
The frame-group selector's readout must be derived live from the selected group each click, so a click updates both the active highlight and the readout text together.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial capture the WebGL vortex with the Frame navigator HUD floating over it at 1440px, 834px and 390px; on mobile the status strip must wrap and stay free of horizontal overflow.
desktop_navigator and mobile_navigator frame the navigator panel itself over the scene; the panel must be legible and well-proportioned, not an overgrown cascade of dark slabs.
desktop_group_pick captures the panel after the visitor selects the Finale frame group in the selector; the readout must update to name Finale, not stay frozen on All frames.
desktop_context_forward and desktop_context_reverse capture the visitor scrolling the vortex forward and reverse; the navigator must persist and carry its fnav--forward / fnav--reverse tag in each.
In the original demo there is no Frame navigator HUD; the panel is the foreground instrument that was added, and the WebGL canvas, atlas, shaders and wheel motion are preserved.

change_completion: The Frame navigator HUD renders with its wordmark, title, four-tile status strip, frame-group row and readout over the scene.
Selecting a frame group updates the readout live to name the chosen group rather than leaving a frozen 'All frames' readout while only the button highlights.
design_consistency: The navigator panel stays legible and well-proportioned over the scene, with contrasting tile text and non-overlapping tiles, preserving the dark glass panel and monospace type.
The navigator persists as one consistent instrument across the initial view and every scroll context, tagged with the matching fnav--<context> class.
regression: The three.js vortex renders full-viewport and the wheel-driven frame motion and 20-image atlas remain functional across all legs.
The 'Frame navigator' wordmark and status-strip labels are preserved by any acceptable solution.
responsive: The 390px and 834px states show no horizontal overflow of the navigator chrome.
The navigator status strip wraps cleanly on mobile so its tiles stack instead of forcing a wide no-wrap row.

author_notes: Repo-grounded three.js/WebGL vortex gallery (J0SUKE/vortex-gallery) built with Vite + TypeScript. The native lever is the gallery's own on-scene Frame navigator HUD (the .fnav panel with a four-tile status strip, frame-group buttons and a live readout). Because the vortex surface is a fixed inset:0 layer with zero scrollWidth, the navigator panel is the sole normal-flow foreground chrome and carries all four graded behaviours: responsive no-overflow of the status strip, legible non-overgrown visual design, cross-context persistence of the panel, and a live frame-group readout. The navigator scroll context is switched deterministically in capture via a window.__vortex hook exposed identically in all legs (infrastructure, not the feature). The WebGL surface renders under swiftshader; the driver's intermittent shader-program parse messages are artifacts, not app errors. The 20 atlas frame images (jpg) are the gallery's own assets. DESIGN_KEYWORDS: vortex, gallery, frame, atlas, navigator, showcase.
